messages:
sam: Heads-up — spotted a reproducible eviction spike in the KV prefix cache when running the replay harness under concurrency. Attaching quick logs and the harness command I used. Need eyes, this looks like a correctness/ordering issue that only shows with replay ordering + multithreading.

anya: Can you paste the exact harness command + config? Is this only on replay or do synthetic generators show it too?

sam: Sure. Command I ran:```bash
./replay_harness --trace /traces/2026-03-01/session_42.json --concurrency 64 --batcher=adaptive --kv-cache=true --kv-capacity=50000
```

Config highlights: ```json
{"batcher":{"type":"adaptive","max_batch_ms":20},"kv":{"enabled":true,"shards":8,"eviction_threshold":0.9}}
```

kevin: What metric shows the regression? hit_rate / p50?

sam: Primary metric is prefix hit_rate. Observed: steady-state hit_rate ~0.87 on synthetic runs. On replay (multithreaded) it collapses to ~0.21 during a 10s warmup ramp. CPU/kernels look healthy (cpu ~70%), latency p50 steady, weirdly no large latency spike.

ryan: Any flamegraphs/profiler outputs?

sam: Small snippet of logs around the spike:```
[03:12:05] kv_eviction: evicted=1200 free=3000 active=48000
[03:12:07] kv_hit: 0.21
[03:12:10] batcher: batch_ms=13 active_batches=3
[03:12:11] kv_insert: key_prefix=usr:msg:abc status=ok
[03:12:11] kv_remove: key_prefix=usr:msg:abc reason=evicted
```

anya: Could be a sharded cache ordering/lock interaction. We switched one shard mutex to try_lock a while back to reduce contention — might allow reordering of inserts vs evictions under heavy concurrency.

sam: I suspected that. Ran controlled tests: 1) synthetic generator (same seq len distribution) multi-threaded -> stable hit_rate ~0.86 2) replay harness single-threaded with original replay order -> stable hit_rate ~0.85 3) replay harness multi-threaded (same parallelism as production) -> hit_rate collapse to ~0.2. So both ordering + concurrency required.

perf-bot: perf-checker: regression detected on commit abc123 (2026-03-12) — KV cache miss rate increased 4.2x specifically when running replay harness with concurrency >=32.

kevin: Can you reproduce with a minimal repro (replay order but two threads) to confirm it's not a 64-thread artifact?

sam: Yes — reproduced at 4 threads already, magnitude scales with threads. Single-threaded replay preserves warmup.

anya: Hypothesis: try_lock allows a thread to skip insertion and later a different thread evicts the same prefix due to stale size accounting. We should ensure insert/evict have a global insertion stamp or use blocking lock for critical section. Also add atomic counters for per-shard occupancy to avoid races.

ryan: Also add per-key sequence/timestamp in the cache metadata (1 integer) to detect ABA eviction (insert A -> evict -> insert B where timestamps show older item removed incorrectly). Instrumentation will make root cause crystal clear.

sam: Quick local patch: switched the try_lock -> lock for insert path and introduced a lightweight per-key version counter. Re-ran the replay harness: eviction spikes reduced ~90%, hit_rate during ramp went from 0.21 -> 0.81. Rough numbers: before: evictions/sec ~1200, after: ~120.

kevin: Nice. Action items: 1) open PR with fix + unit test reproducer 2) add nightly canary that runs replay harness against dedicated canary pool 3) add metric kv_eviction_rate_by_concurrency to datadog.

sam: Will open PR. Also adding a short explainer to the benchmark playbook about this footgun: replay ordering + concurrency can exercise different code paths than synthetic RPS. Link to trace used: https://s3.redwood/traces/session_42.json

anya: Adding "release-blocker" label if the PR touches core locking primitives (makes sense for a high-risk bug).

ryan: Parallel note — update the benchmark methodology doc: always run both synthetic and replay with a seeded deterministic ordering and a sweep of concurrency values (1,2,4,8,16,32,64). Document the expected hit-rate tolerances.

sam: Agreed. I'll include a small reproducer in the PR that runs in CI (flaky allowed but gated behind a separate job). PR will include the harness command above and the failing trace snippet.

kevin: Thanks. Ping us when PR is up and we can run a dedicated canary.

sam: Will do :thumbsup:

(edited)
